dataset: Washington energy prices and chiller-plant efficiency behind the Savings tab defaults: natural gas ($/MMBtu) for heating, electricity ($/kWh) and whole-plant kW/ton for cooling. Every figure is copied from the source page as served on the access date; conversions are shown.

conventions.gas_conversion: EIA prices gas in $ per thousand cubic feet (Mcf). $/MMBtu = $/Mcf ÷ (heat content Btu/cf ÷ 1000). 2025 U.S. heat content of gas delivered to consumers = 1,036 Btu/cf (P4), so $/MMBtu = $/Mcf ÷ 1.036.
conventions.kw_per_ton: 1 ton of refrigeration = 12,000 Btu/hr; kWh = Btu ÷ 12,000 × kW/ton.

default_chosen.why: Rounded Washington commercial average (EIA 2025 $13.80, 2026 Jan–Jul $14.56); PSE Schedule 31 averages $14.72. The former $8 default matched only interruptible service.
Washington commercial average 11.78¢ (EIA, July 2026). PSE commercial schedules average $0.16–0.21/kWh; the statewide figure is lowered by public hydro utilities.

chiller_plant.quote: Whereas a typical packaged cooling unit has an efficiency of 1.1 to 1.4 kW/ton, a chiller-based system can have a full load efficiency that is far lower—values of 0.8 to 1.0 kW/ton for the entire chiller plant are typical.

default_chosen.why: Middle of the 0.8–1.0 kW/ton whole-plant range (chillers, pumps, cooling tower). The former 0.75 sat near chiller-only ratings.
